claims.title: Continuous moment-encoder rigidity
claims.claimed_result_or_task: Every continuous exact planar encoder has form c+u*s+v*phi(s), with real-independent u,v; converse exactness also holds.
claims.scope: K>=4; phi continuous on [-1,1], C1 in its interior and nonaffine; psi continuous, interior C1, strictly convex or strictly concave; f=mean(phi)-psi(mean).
claims.criterion: Exact computation; positive squared score implies this prerequisite.
claims.status: included; internally reviewed under stated hypotheses
claims.priority_audit: Charalambides (2013), Theorem 1.6 and Section 5, is a close affine-uniqueness and regularization precedent. Distinction retained: scalar exactness and one-way collision implication yield local factorization; C1 nonaffine features may have affine subintervals. Historical priority not established.

claims.title: General fixed-encoder small-noise MSE and paired comparisons
claims.claimed_result_or_task: For the specified strip/readout decoder, MSE/N0 tends to tr(Q_pi G^-1)/(2 K^2). For orthogonal polynomial features p=2 or4 this specializes to [1/b^2+p^2 E(m^(2p-2))/a^2]/(2 K^2 P), retaining eq:small-noise-mse. The existing study evaluates 72 paired finite-noise conditions.
claims.scope: Exact-score and synthesis hypotheses; fixed joint source law independent of proper complex Gaussian noise, |m|<1 almost surely, Q_pi=E[w(m)w(m)^T] positive definite. Source coordinates need not be independent. Optional scalar output clipping requires the true target strictly inside its interval almost surely. The empirical study retains its stated independent-source priors.
claims.criterion: Specified-decoder small-noise coefficient and separate finite-noise empirical comparisons; no unrestricted estimator or finite-noise optimality claim.
claims.proof_status: General dominated-convergence argument internally reviewed; source moments and selected coefficients reproduced by a second implementation in the same environment.
claims.priority_audit: Do not interchange the fixed-encoder small-noise limit with optimization over noise-dependent encoders. Finite-SNR results need not agree with the limit within Monte Carlo uncertainty.
claims.finite_snr_qualification: At K=4 with endpoint-Beta sources, the recorded 30-dB MSE/N0 values remain 3.49%-7.19% below the asymptotic coefficient, approximately 9.6-10.5 reported Monte Carlo standard errors away. The implemented clipping remains relevant at finite noise.

claims.title: Equivalent six-variable inverse-metric synthesis
claims.claimed_result_or_task: Minimize t over symmetric 2x2 X, center a in R2, and t, subject to peak-block LMIs and w_sigma^T X w_sigma<=t. The optimum is positive and attained; Lambda_sq_star=K^2/t_star. Reconstruct U^T U=X^-1 and E(s)=U(g(s)-a).
claims.scope: Exact-score and global-synthesis hypotheses; nonaffine feature graph and pointwise P>0. Six real variables and a continuum of peak-block inequalities.
claims.criterion: Squared separation, equivalently maximum inverse-metric endpoint sensitivity.
claims.priority_audit: Equivalent enclosing-ellipse formulation using classical Schur-complement modeling. Nonaffineness excludes singular X; endpoint budgets and a fixed peak block control sublevels. Do not claim novelty of SDP/ellipsoid tools or elimination of continuum constraints.
claims.status: included; internally reviewed under stated hypotheses
claims.proof_status: Internal mathematical review within the writing workflow; no invalidating defect found.

claims.title: Global robustness-constrained small-noise frontier
claims.claimed_result_or_task: The minimum specified-decoder small-noise coefficient over all continuous exact peak-admissible encoders under Lambda_sq>=K^2 gamma equals a five-variable convex inverse-metric program. It attains its optimum, has a unique optimal feature metric, and has a finite continuous convex nondecreasing value. A plateau ends at the unconstrained optimum actual floor; beyond it the floor is active and the value strictly increases.
claims.scope: TIT-15 hypotheses with positive-definite Q_pi and fixed source law; gamma in [0,lambda_star]. At gamma=0 omit endpoint budgets. Five real variables and continuous peak-block inequalities. Translation need not be unique.
claims.criterion: Specified-decoder leading Gaussian-MSE coefficient subject to a worst-case squared-separation floor.
claims.priority_audit: Strict convexity and convexity in the floor use the equivalent Gram formulation, not linearity of the inverse objective alone. Q_pi positive definite gives compact objective sublevels. The theorem does not optimize finite-noise risk over all estimators or interchange a limit with noise-dependent optimization.
claims.status: included; internally reviewed under stated hypotheses
claims.proof_status: Internal mathematical review within the writing workflow; no invalidating defect found.

claims.title: Explicit quadratic robustness-small-noise tradeoff
claims.claimed_result_or_task: For quadratic features, choose b_gamma=min(b_eff,b_plus(gamma/P)), where b_eff minimizes the prior-averaged sensitivity and b_plus is the upper robustness-boundary root. The curve sqrt(P)[sqrt(b_gamma(2-b_gamma))*s+i(b_gamma*s^2-1)] achieves the global continuous-encoder frontier.
claims.scope: TIT-17 hypotheses; phi(s)=s^2, even strictly convex/concave C1 readout, symmetric mean distribution; 0<M_eff<M. Explicitly classified full continuous exact encoder class for K>=4.
claims.criterion: Specified-decoder leading Gaussian-MSE coefficient under prescribed squared separation.
claims.priority_audit: Reflection and peak-boundary domination justify reduction to the one-parameter family before scalar minimization. Numerical optimization comparisons are not exact certificates. Selected independent checks validate values, not the universal theorem or its originality.
claims.status: included; internally reviewed under stated hypotheses
claims.proof_status: Internal mathematical review within the writing workflow; no invalidating defect found.

claims.title: Deterministic implementation and residual-channel error bounds
claims.claimed_result_or_task: The ideal decoder obeys |error|<=L_E (|N|+K epsilon sqrt(P)+sqrt(P) sum_k |d_k|) for a peak-feasible implemented encoder uniformly within epsilon sqrt(P) of E and residual gains 1+d_k. Contracting before quantization ensures peak feasibility with epsilon<=2r. Retaining eta of optimal squared separation increases the uniform amplification budget by at most eta^(-1/2).
claims.scope: Fixed ideal encoder and its global Lipschitz decoder; implemented map remains pointwise peak-admissible. Residual errors may add coherently. The stated scalar-quantizer example requires r=sqrt(2)/(2^B-1)<1, hence integer B>=2.
claims.criterion: Uniform deterministic error bound, separate from exact representation and finite-noise optimum.
claims.priority_audit: Direct triangle-inequality application of the existing sharp decoder bound. K does not suppress the normalized worst-case coherent encoder/gain errors. Does not extend exact rigidity to mismatched, asynchronous, or user-specific channels.
claims.status: included; internally reviewed under stated hypotheses
claims.proof_status: Internal mathematical review within the writing workflow; no invalidating defect found.

claims.title: Qualitative approximate rigidity under compactness
claims.claimed_result_or_task: For a fixed target, peak bound, common encoder continuity modulus, and decoder Lipschitz budget L, vanishing uniform computation error forces uniform distance to the nondegenerate affine-feature family to vanish. A nondecreasing error-to-distance modulus exists, without an explicit rate.
claims.scope: Exact rigidity hypotheses and K>=4; peak-admissible continuous encoders in a class with one fixed continuity modulus; a globally L-Lipschitz decoder for each encoder; uniform target error.
claims.criterion: Qualitative convergence of encoder-family distance under approximate computation.
claims.priority_audit: Arzela-Ascoli compactness plus the limiting pairwise collision inequality and exact rigidity. The feature family is nonclosed, but its distance function is continuous and the limiting encoder is nondegenerate. No quantitative rate, average-MSE implication, unrestricted conditioning bound, or necessity of added hypotheses is claimed.
